findings.conclusion: Section 2.4 expressly allows macOS applications and libraries to be distributed without a separate written agreement, subject to compliance. Section 2.2A distinguishes macOS from other Apple SDKs. This does not approve this addon, imply App Store distribution rights or authorize redistribution of SDK components.

SDK definitions cover headers/APIs/libraries; section 2.7 reserves redistribution and derivative-work rights subject to stated permission/OSS/sample-code exceptions. Section 2.5 retains notices for permitted copies, not a standalone copying grant. Do not bundle SDK headers, .tbd, frameworks, SDK tools or SDK source on this review alone.

The public PDF is a dated snapshot, not proof of which terms a future builder accepted or which SDK generated the bindings. Distinguish redistributable macOS application/library object code from SDK-derived declarations/source. Upstream MIT/Apache/Zlib terms cannot by themselves establish Apple rights. No applicable-law enforceability or copyrightability opinion is made.

obligations: Include existing copyright notices and entire Boost statement when redistributing source/covered material.
The exception applies only when such copies/derivative works are solely machine-executable object code generated by a source language processor; do not presume every mixed npm/Bun archive qualifies.

Conservative future packaging plan: retain full exact license/notices even with object code, without relying on the exception. No duty to publish proprietary source is imposed by the inspected BSL text.
Preserve Copyright © 2015, Simonas Kazlauskas and the ISC permission notice in all copies; preserve full license/disclaimer in future license assets.
No binary-only notice exception appears in the inspected text. No source-disclosure condition is stated.
A MIT/Apache choice does not remove the conjunctive Unicode obligation.

Retain Copyright © 1991-2023 Unicode, Inc. and permission notice with all copies OR associated documentation; ship full LICENSE-UNICODE in future distribution materials rather than relying on an external link alone.
Do not use the copyright-holder name to advertise/promote without prior written authorization, except as contained in the notice.
